country.comment: Primary empirical/regulatory case study focuses on Alabama (specifically four Black Belt counties: Hale, Lowndes, Perry, and Wilcox, with focal analysis of Uniontown in Perry County) in the United States, preceded by comparative constitutional and historical discussion of Western Europe and North America.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 9-20, Sections 5-6; Table 1, PDF p. 12

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive legal-regulatory and environmental case study with no inferential regression or statistical effect size reported. Secondary statistics from cited studies (e.g., Elliott et al. 2017; McKenna et al. 2017; MacDonald et al. 2011) are also reviewed in Sections 5-6.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative / descriptive regulatory case study — no statistical effect estimate reported. Constitutional review finds zero constitutions in Western Europe or English-speaking North America recognizing a human right to water or sanitation (only Mexico in North America). In the focal Uniontown, Perry County, Alabama wastewater case study, despite an initial 2002 violation notice, a 2005 civil action, a 2008 binding consent decree to eliminate sanitary sewer overflows within 3 years, and 76 non-compliance citations between 2005 and 2018, ADEM reissued NPDES discharge permits in 2008 and 2012 and approved an unsuitable second spray field on low-permeability clay soil before issuing a March 2014 Stop Work order (after $4.4 million in USDA grants were spent); chronic overflows persisted 11 years post-decree, releasing >=1.25 million gallons from the treatment lagoon into Cottonwood Creek (Dec 2017-Jan 2019) and >1 million gallons from the spray field into Freetown Creek in 2018, with March 24, 2018 overflow samples containing 7,300-11,000 cfu/100 ml of E. coli (exceeding the 4,000 cfu/100 ml NPDES permit daily maximum and 3,200 cfu/100 ml state surface water limit).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section 1; PDF p. 6, Section 3; PDF pp. 14-19, Section 6; Figure 1, PDF p. 16

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling is 2 (non-experimental legal-institutional case study). Assigned 2 because the author directly documents the legal and regulatory mechanisms operating in practice using primary ADEM administrative enforcement records (notices of violation, 2005 civil complaint, 2008 consent decree, 2008/2012 NPDES permit reissuances, 2014 Stop Work order, 2016-2019 sanitary sewer overflow filings), USEPA diagnostic reports, municipal engineering filings, and direct field observations/water sampling.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 14-19, Section 6; Figure 1, PDF p. 16

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines regulatory enforcement collapse and non-enforcement of violations, industrial discharge permits, and administrative stop-work orders (ENFORCEMENT, sanction), unfulfilled civil litigation and a 2008 binding consent decree (judicial_review), citizen pollution and civil complaints (complaint), poor municipal/regional wastewater planning and municipal water boundary exclusion (ELIGIBILITY, planning, service_area), and fragmented/uncoordinated oversight across municipal, state (ADEM), and federal (USEPA) authorities (institutional_fragmentation).
mechanism_flags.value: ENFORCEMENT, ELIGIBILITY, sanction, judicial_review, complaint, planning, service_area, institutional_fragmentation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 10-11, Section 5; PDF pp. 14-20, Section 6

outcome_flags.comment: Focuses on household and municipal sanitation/sewer provision (sanitation_access), safe water access (water_access), microbial/chemical water contamination and raw sewage overflows (service_quality), exclusion from centralized municipal water/sewer networks and unpermitted household sewage connections (formal_connection), and water poverty/affordability in comparative background (affordability).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 9-11, Section 5; PDF pp. 12-19, Section 6; Figure 1, PDF p. 16

publication_year.comment: Published in Azafea. Revista de Filosofía, Vol. 21, 2019 (received March 29, 2019; accepted June 28, 2019).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and reception/acceptance dates

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Study combines political-philosophical and comparative constitutional analysis with an empirical legal-regulatory case study grounded in administrative enforcement dockets (ADEM violations, consent decree, NPDES permits, stop-work order, overflow filings, USEPA diagnostic report), fitting the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework rather than conventional epidemiological or interview-based qualitative checklists.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Section 1; PDF pp. 11-20, Section 6

sample_size.comment: No formal sampling frame or sample size N is reported because the article is a political-philosophy and constitutional essay paired with a regulatory case study (comparing 4 Alabama Black Belt counties in Table 1 — Hale, Lowndes, Perry, and Wilcox — and focusing in depth on 1 municipal wastewater system, Uniontown WWTP in Perry County, Alabama, using ADEM eFile records, 76 non-compliance citations from 2005-2018, 2017-2019 sanitary sewer overflow reports, and March 24, 2018 water samples of unstated N).
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; Table 1, PDF p. 12; PDF pp. 13-19, Section 6

study_design.comment: Author explicitly frames the paper as beginning with political philosophy (including comparative constitutional and historical review) and ending with a case study in Alabama evaluating regulatory and municipal failure in Uniontown's wastewater system via administrative records, engineering reports, and field/water quality observations.
study_design.value: Political-philosophical and comparative constitutional analysis combined with a documentary legal-regulatory case study (administrative enforcement records, engineering reports, and field observations/water sampling)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF pp. 11-19, Section 6

evidence_quotes.quote: In fact, there are no constitutions from Western Europe or English-speaking North America that address human rights to water or sanitation (Dobbins, unpublished manuscript, 2019).

evidence_quotes.criterion: country and study_design (Alabama Black Belt case study)
evidence_quotes.quote: Alabama, particularly the “Black Belt” of Alabama, provides a model for the nexus of race, economics, governmental competence or malfeasance, and regulatory failure in the provision of water and sanitation.

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect_estimate and mechanism_certainty (consent decree non-compliance and chronic overflows)
evidence_quotes.quote: Uniontown is an exceptional model of systemic failure because both the lagoon and the spray field continue spilling contaminated water into two disparate creeks, and fouling two watersheds, for 11 years after a binding consent decree to eliminate sanitary sewer overflows within three years (ADEM, 2008a).

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect_estimate and outcome_flags (service_quality / E. coli contamination)
evidence_quotes.quote: On March 24th, water samples from one of these overflows contained between 7,300 and 11,000 colony-forming units of Escheria coli in 100 ml (cfu/100ml) (Dobbins, unpublished data).

evidence_quotes.criterion: mechanism_flags and mechanism_certainty (regulatory citations, civil complaint, consent decree, and permit reissuance)
evidence_quotes.quote: From 2005 to 2018, there were 76 additional citations for non-compliance in Uniontown sewer system (ADEM efile). Despite these continuing violations, an on-going civil action complaint (ADEM, 2005) and a consent decree in which Uniontown agreed to fix its problems within 3 years (ADEM, 2008a) a discharge permit was reissued to the Uniontown WWTP in 2008 (ADEM, 2008b) and 2012 (ADEM, 2012).
